sources.title: William Crooke, The Popular Religion and Folk-Lore of Northern India, volume 1 (1896)
sources.limitations: Colonial-era collection: records beliefs through historical biases, caste hierarchies and outsider terminology. Directly consulted sections Airi and The Bhut; cited earlier authorities were not independently inspected.

sources.title: Lal Behari Dey, Folk-tales of Bengal: The Story of a Brahmadaitya
sources.limitations: A particular collected tale and its footnote; not a universal description of all regional Brahmadaitya traditions. Historical caste hierarchy is part of the narrative, not endorsed here.

sources.title: If you hear calls at night don’t look back: Exploring stories of Nishir Daak
sources.limitations: Mixes anecdote, literary stories and paranormal assertions; records reported beliefs, not demonstrated events. References are not independently verified.

sources.title: Jilaiya
sources.limitations: Very short entry. Cites Bonnerjea, A Dictionary of Superstitions and Mythology (1920); that underlying work was not inspected.

sources.title: Masan
sources.limitations: Brief historical description using caste categories. Cited Bonnerjea (1920) was not inspected; not a comprehensive account of regional Masan traditions.

sources.title: Quran 27:39, in context 27:38–40
sources.limitations: The verse establishes an ifrit among the jinn and a particular offer to Solomon; it does not supply a universal anatomy, Indian locality or species taxonomy.

sources.title: Quran 37:7
sources.limitations: The adjective translated rebellious does not by itself establish a separate species of jinn.

sources.title: Quran 55:15
